newsitem.title: POLAND: Budapest leads E.Europe bourses after record surge.
newsitem.headline: Budapest leads E.Europe bourses after record surge.

text.p: The Budapest bourse led other East European exchanges this week, surging to all-time highs in heavy volume, and Prague and Warsaw were also lifted by foreign buying.
Bratislava and Bucharest slipped, while Zagreb stocks firmed on Friday .
BUDAPEST

The Hungarian market outpaced rising European markets and continued its year-end rally, closing at its seventh successive record on Friday and also breaking the 4,000 point barrier for the first time.
On Friday the BUX index closed at 4,096.52 points, up a massive 278.31 points over last Friday.
The fact the Fed left its rates steady on Tuesday was only one factor behind the accelerated rally, analysts said.
Moody's said on Thursday that it had upgraded the sovereign ceiling for foreign currency debt of Hungary to Baa3 from Ba1, providing a fresh boost.
"I would say the reason behind the rally is that Moody's upgrading urged everybody to buy more stocks on the market which enjoys enormous investor confidence," Peter Lencs of MKB Securities said.
PRAGUE
Czech shares, especially major issues, pushed ahead on the week with SPT Telecom, the most heavily weighted stock, taking the lead, though dealers could not explain why.
SPT Telecom, which accounts for over 20 percent of the PX50's capitalisation, gained more than six percent before falling slightly on Friday.
Dealers said SPT had benefited from buying by foreign investors hesitating in recent weeks due to fears of a lack of transparency in the capital markets.
WARSAW

Polish shares on Friday rose for the fourth straight session and analysts said the higher turnover and stronger buying after price fixing suggested the market might be breaking out of its seven-week flat trend.
Analysts said investors might be buying in advance of an anticipated repeat of last year's January growth despite some relatively fresh negative signals.

"It seems if the market is rising despite weak (November) earnings and a threat of an interest rate rise, we could be entering a growth trend," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed on Friday at 14,051.0 points, up 344.7 points or percent from last Friday.
ZAGREB

Croatian stocks closed the week on a firmer tone and trading also revived as investors returned briefly ahead of Christmas holidays. Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva led other issues up.
As their GDRs recovered in London, Pliva gained 600 kuna to end the week at 13,600 and Zagrebacka closed at 1,020 kuna -- up 40 from last Friday.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) saw large volumes traded in main issues during the year's last trading week, but brokers said most of them were in previously-agreed block and direct trades.
The 12-share SAX index eased 3.04 points to close the year at 178.05 on Thursday from Monday's open at 181.09 points.
"What we saw this week were mostly only portfolio swaps, usual for the period before the end of year," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.
He said investors next month might show optimism after several months of lethargy mainly due to legislative moves such as the draft of an amendment to the securities law.
BUCHAREST

Volumes stayed light on the Bucharest bourse this week with investors already in a holiday mood. On Thursday, turnover rose by 14 million lei, but stayed low at 40 million, while prices were mixed, sending two independent indices to new year lows.
Buying interest at the week's two sessions focused on Azomures SA fertiliser maker, which took the bulk of turnover and closed 500 lei stronger at 12,100 on Thursday.
The bourse's next trading session starts on January 7.
Two unofficial indices, the VAB and the BIG, slipped by 1.7 percent from the previous session to year lows of 262 points and 261.36 points respectively.
